title: Automated Cost-Tuning: RBAC & Audit Trail for Auto-Apply and Safe Rollback
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a compliance-first control plane for the Cost Optimization Automation feature (batching + KV-prefix caching suggestions) so that auto-apply and automated rollback are auditable, role-restricted, and safe for enterprise customers. This ticket covers RBAC rules, approval flows, immutable audit events, change-write pathways, and an automated safe-rollback mechanism integrated with the Console and the runtime.

Context: The Optimize engine generates recommended config deltas (batch sizes, cache rules, quantization profiles). We already have a pilot auto-apply path that can push these deltas directly to runtime config. Customers with stringent security/compliance requirements have asked for: (1) fine-grained role controls over who can opt-in/out of auto-apply, (2) an auditable change history with tamper-evidence and exportable artifacts, and (3) a deterministic, fast rollback path that can be triggered automatically on regressions or manually by an operator with the correct role.

Scope: This work includes: (A) RBAC primitives for Optimize actions (recommend, apply, schedule-apply, cancel-apply, force-rollback), (B) Change management workflow (manual approvals, timeboxed automatic approvals, audit annotations), (C) Write-once append-only audit log for all generated recommendations and state transitions, (D) Safe-rollback orchestration that captures pre-change snapshots and provides deterministic revert steps, (E) Console UX hooks for approvals and audit visibility, and (F) API and infra for retention and export (S3/Customer-S3).

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement cost-model tuning heuristics, nor does it touch model quantization engine internals. It assumes the Optimize engine already outputs validated deltas and scoring metadata.
acceptance_criteria: RBAC: new roles and permissions exist and are enforced for Optimize actions (recommend_view, recommend_apply, recommend_approve, recommend_rollback). Enforcement verified via API tests and Console integration.

Audit trail: every recommendation lifecycle event (generated -> proposed -> approved -> applied -> rolled_back) is recorded in an append-only audit log with actor, timestamp, delta payload, prior snapshot reference, and signed hash for tamper detection.

Change snapshots: before any auto-apply, the runtime config snapshot is stored and linked to the audit event. Rollback uses that snapshot to restore settings within 30s for a typical runtime pool (measured on staging).

Approval workflows: Console shows pending approvals for scheduled applies; users with recommend_approve can approve with comments. Timeboxed auto-approve config honored when enabled and only for customers who opted in.
CLI/API parity: all apply/rollback flows available via API/CLI with the same RBAC checks and audit outcomes as the Console flows.
Export: customers can export audit events for a rolling 90-day window to S3 in newline-delimited JSON format.
Security review: architecture notes and threat model reviewed and signed off by Security team (ticket ENG-11670 referenced).

updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting. Identified three acceptance gates: RBAC enforcement, immutable audit log, snapshot-based rollback. Action: design RBAC mapping and audit schema.
2026-02-18: Security reviewed initial threat model. Feedback: require signed event hash and retention TTL configuration per customer. (See ENG-11670).

2026-02-25: Prototype audit log implemented as append-only table. Found performance bottleneck on high-frequency recommendations - switched to batched append with single transaction per batch. Open PR linked.
2026-03-03: UX mockups posted to Confluence. PM requested an explicit 'simulate apply' button that writes to audit log but does not change runtime. Added as a task.

2026-03-09: Integration test for snapshot+rollback passed on staging for a 4-node pool with median restore time 22s. Noted race condition when concurrent manual edits occur; mitigation: optimistic lock via config version and reject auto-apply if version mismatch.
2026-03-12: Internal security sign-off pending on key management for event signing. Proposal: use KMS asymmetric signing per-tenant. Waiting on Infra design feedback (INF-682).
risks_mitigation: Concurrent edits: optimistic version check + reject-and-requeue auto-applies with admin notification.
Tampering of logs: signed event hashes stored in KMS-backed key rotation; retention immutability enforced by write-once S3 bucket when configured.
False positives in rollback detection: configurable thresholds and a simulation mode to validate restores before enabling automatic rollback in a customer account.
Performance overhead: batch audit writes and async indexing to keep tail latency low for the runtime control plane.
Operational blast radius: default auto-apply is disabled for enterprise accounts; enablement requires approval from two distinct roles (admin + infra-operator).
